title: A synovial joint lets bones move inside a fluid-filled cavity
summary: OpenStax says a synovial joint lets bones move freely against each other inside a cavity of lubricating fluid.
body: OpenStax says synovial joints are the most common joints. The bone surfaces are not stuck directly together. They meet inside a joint cavity. Articular cartilage and synovial fluid reduce friction. Ligaments hold the bones together and resist excessive movement. A freely movable joint of this kind is called a diarthrosis. The elbow and knee are hinge examples on the page. This card is how a movable joint is built. It is not a treatment for a sprain.

sources.title: 9.1 and 9.4, chapter review
